acceptance_threshold: parquet opens; expected timestamp columns present.
canonical_contract: app.connect.tlc_trips maps these onto ServiceRequest (ADR-0011); app.replay.teardown consumes them as VehicleSegments (ADR-0039).
derived_artifacts: GOVERNANCE-ONLY MANIFEST (platform/tools/build_realdata_manifests.py). These bytes were hand-acquired before the governed estate existed and live at the paths below. Nothing was moved, copied or re-downloaded, and NO .acquired.json record is written -- this dataset did not go through app.estate.acquire, and claiming it did would forge the provenance the estate exists to make trustworthy.
geography: New York City, TLC taxi zones.
license_and_commercial_rights: NYC TLC publishes trip records as open data for public use, including commercial use, with no registration or key. Records are trip-level but contain NO rider identifier, name, or precise origin/destination address -- TLC publishes zone-level pickup/dropoff only.
owner_and_source: New York City Taxi & Limousine Commission (TLC) trip record data. Acquired by hand into realdata/raw_tlc/ and realdata/raw_tlc_taxi/ before the governed estate existed.
retention_and_deletion: cheaply reproducible from the public source -- these raw files are gitignored and may be deleted to reclaim space (~57 GB) without losing evidence, since the committed artifacts derived from them carry their own hashes.
schema_and_format: Apache Parquet, one file per month per service. FHVHV carries request/on-scene/pickup/dropoff timestamps, which is what makes the ADR-0039 deadhead teardown possible on real public data.
time_coverage: monthly Parquet files; FHVHV from 2019 onward, yellow/green longer.
update_frequency: monthly upstream; the local copy is a static snapshot.
